claim: CMP 170HX cards enumerate as PCI device 10de:20c2, expose CUDA compute capability 8.0, and report 65,536 MiB of HBM after the community unlock path is applied.
stance_target: the repo's premise that five cards provide 320 GB of usable HBM2e (64 GB x 5)
scope_conditions: PixelML/club-170hx four-card rig; Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 6.8, driver 610.43.03, pinned cmpunlocker; measured 2026-08-30
quoted_support: The cards tested by this project enumerate as PCI device `10de:20c2`, expose CUDA compute capability 8.0, and report 65,536 MiB after the community unlock path is working.

claim: The CMP 170HX has no NVLink, so every multi-card collective crosses PCIe and can dominate runtime; the card is explicitly not equivalent to a supported A100.
stance_target: the repo's claim that the fabric, not the compute, is the binding constraint on multi-card training
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX rig, any multi-card workload
quoted_support: | No NVLink  | Multi-card collectives cross PCIe and can dominate runtime  | ... It does not make it equivalent to a supported A100

claim: With the cmpunlocker link patch all four cards on the club's 4-card PLX host train PCIe Gen2 x16, and Gen3 is unreachable because the OPT_DISABLE_GEN3_SPEED fuse reads 1 on every card checked.
stance_target: the repo's premise that the box is limited to PCIe Gen2 x4 — on this particular host the negotiated width is x16, so every communication number derived from x4 is 4x pessimistic for this rig
scope_conditions: 4-card PLX host (dual-socket Broadwell Xeon E5-2686 v4, two PLX PEX 8747 switches, two cards per switch); cmpunlocker link patch applied; measured 2026-10-01/02
quoted_support: **Update 2026-10-02 (measured):** the Gen1 ceiling below is the _stock_ driver's. With the cmpunlocker link patch all four cards on the 4-card PLX host train **Gen2 x16** ; Gen3 is blocked by the `OPT_DISABLE_GEN3_SPEED` fuse, which reads 1 on every card we checked.

claim: On the stock driver every card advertises LnkCap 2.5GT/s x16 (PCIe Gen1), and a card in a bifurcated slot training at x8 is at that slot's ceiling rather than a riser or passthrough fault.
stance_target: the link-width question: Gen1 x16 is the stock advertised maximum, so a Gen1 link seen in a guest is a card/vBIOS capability, not a hypervisor bug
scope_conditions: Hypervisor-side lspci -vv on the four-card test node, stock driver, measured 2026-09-02
quoted_support: Host-side `lspci -vv` on the hypervisor shows every CMP 170HX card advertising `LnkCap: Speed 2.5GT/s, Width x16`. PCIe Gen1 is the card's advertised maximum, so a Gen1 link seen in a guest is a card/vBIOS capability, not a hypervisor passthrough bug. One card trains at x8 instead of the advertised x16.

claim: The club's four-card rig had validated CUDA enumeration, a 16 GiB cross-window write/read smoke test and post-load health checks on three cards, but four-card workload performance remained untested at the time of writing.
stance_target: the evidentiary base for any multi-card throughput claim on this hardware — capacity and enumeration are measured, aggregate multi-card throughput is not
scope_conditions: Ubuntu 22.04, Linux 6.8, driver 610.43.03, pinned unlocker; four-card open-frame chassis
quoted_support: **Measured:** three cards passed CUDA enumeration, a 16 GiB cross-window write/read smoke test, an SM kernel, and post-load health checks ... Four-card workload performance remains untested.
